ideas.title: Printed indoor routes keep museum visitors satisfied during weather closures
ideas.description: Show how a free sculpture route gives visitors a satisfying fallback when a flooded garden is closed. In the museum's two April openings, the front desk issued 38 printed routes.
ideas.audience: Museum visitors planning to see the sculpture garden
ideas.rationale: The handout count demonstrates that the substitute route protects the visitor experience. The museum can use the story to explain the indoor option during temporary closures.
ideas.evidence: The museum handed out 38 printed routes at two April Sunday openings. The route follows step-free public corridors from the desk to the café.

ideas.title: A pilot without measurement: the museum distributed an alternative route but didn't track whether it worked
ideas.description: The museum ran a small, on‑the‑ground pilot—handing out a free printed indoor route when the sculpture garden closed for high water—but staff recorded distribution counts only and did not measure route completion or visitor satisfaction, limiting what can be learned from the experiment.
ideas.audience: Museum operations managers, visitor experience leads, program evaluators at cultural institutions
ideas.rationale: This idea highlights a concrete operational learning: running a pilot without clear success metrics prevents evidence‑based decisions about whether the intervention should be refined, repeated, or scaled. It matters to readers who run visitor experiments because it shows how easy it is to miss the evaluation step even when a feasible intervention is deployed. Gaps & uncertainty: the source documents the absence of systematic completion and satisfaction tracking but does not state whether informal feedback was collected or whether any internal follow‑up evaluation was planned.
ideas.evidence: Explicit facts: the museum handed out the route at two wet Sunday openings and the desk counted 38 copies handed out; “staff recorded no systematic counts of how many visitors completed the route and did not track visitor satisfaction.”

ideas.title: When high water closes the sculpture garden, pick up an indoor route
ideas.description: Help visitors adjust their plans with the free printed route through the permanent indoor sculpture galleries. It starts at the front desk, follows step-free public corridors and ends at the café. Visitors should check the same-day garden notice before travelling.
ideas.audience: Museum visitors planning to see the sculpture garden
ideas.rationale: The indoor route gives those visitors a practical alternative during a high-water closure, while the same-day notice helps them plan their visit.
ideas.evidence: The visitor note describes the free front-desk route, its endpoints and step-free corridors. It asks visitors to check the same-day notice and describes the route as an alternative during a high-water closure.
